data.standardized_narrative: Using the gross claims development triangle the syndicate experienced an aggregate favourable prior-year development (release) of approximately 8.0 million (reporting currency) in 2021, representing about a 4.6% release versus opening gross claims outstanding. The report also contains a narrative (net, GBP-denominated) stating a GBP 2.626m deterioration on prior year reserves; however no explicit gross prior year movement figure is provided, so the triangle-derived gross release is used here. The syndicate writes reinsurance (treated as 'Treaty') and prior-year movements were concentrated in older underwriting years (2017-2019). The report highlights uncertainty due to reliance on cedant reserving data (notably AXA XL) and reinsurance recoveries and IBNR estimation as contributing factors.
raw_causal_phrases: This reliance and lack of source data adds an extra layer of uncertainty in relation to estimating claims provisions.

The two most critical assumptions as regards claims provisions are that the past is a reasonable predictor of the likely level of claims development and that the rating and other models used for current business are fair reflections of the likely level of ultimate claims to be incurred.
In 2021, there has been an overall deterioration of GBP 2,626k on prior year reserves (2020: deficit GBP 11,576k).
data.data_quality_notes: Gross prior-year movement was not explicitly presented as a single 'movement in prior year provision' gross figure. A gross prior-year movement was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (confidence 0.8) giving a net release of ~8.013m USD. The report also contains a conflicting narrative net GBP figure ("overall deterioration of GBP 2,626k") which is net of reinsurance and in GBP; no gross GBP or USD PYD was explicitly disclosed. The triangle may be affected by cedant bordereaux and RITC activity (2019 RITC noted) which can distort development calculations.
